headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP and browser access can leak or misroute document data when paired with local-only marker, while shared-input trust creates prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest untrusted document content or tool output. marker is a document processor with no listed isolation or provenance controls, so if its outputs are fed into LightAgent, instruction-like text could be treated as trusted. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF marker output is copied or piped into LightAgent prompts or MCP inputs
IF LightAgent parses document text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and system prompt that treats marker text as untrusted
Strip executable-looking directives from marker output before reuse
Require manual review before any LightAgent tool call based on marker text
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between marker and LightAgent

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and has broad network egress; marker is a document processor with no declared data classes or network egress. If the pair shares files or prompts, sensitive document contents can flow into LightAgent and then out over its network path. The evidence is indirect, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF marker processes sensitive documents that are then passed to LightAgent
IF LightAgent sends those contents through its OpenAI-compatible APIs or MCP tools
mitigations: Keep marker and LightAgent on separate workspaces
Disable LightAgent network egress for sensitive runs
Redact sensitive fields before handing marker output to LightAgent
Use local-only test documents first
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and can write via tools indirectly, while marker explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main risk is LightAgent overwriting shared artifacts if both are pointed at the same directory. marker’s lack of write capability keeps the blast radius small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same writable directory
IF LightAgent is given file-write or git-adjacent tools in the surrounding orchestrator
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one LightAgent instance per workspace
Make marker outputs read-only
Check in a backup before shared edits
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state that marker may consume as document input. If marker renders or transforms LightAgent output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions. Because marker is a document processor and not an action agent, the blast radius is narrower than high, but the pathway exists.
conditions: IF marker ingests LightAgent-generated text or citations as authoritative input
IF LightAgent output contains hallucinated facts or malformed provenance
mitigations: Require human review of LightAgent outputs before marker uses them
Validate citations and structured fields before ingestion
Keep a source-of-truth file separate from generated drafts
Use a checksum or diff step between agents
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles API keys, conversations, memory, and trace data, while marker’s profile lists no touched data classes or special residency/compliance constraints. The pair does not show a documented residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is visible from the profiles. The other agent is not cited beyond its empty data-class surface because no specific mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or personal data is processed through LightAgent
IF marker is used in a workflow that requires retention or deletion controls not documented here
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to LightAgent
Document retention expectations for generated artifacts
Store secrets outside prompts and documents
Review vendor terms before production use
requires-engineering: add compliance logging and deletion workflows
